persona: Katarzyna (Kasia) Nowak, support operations lead at Rowerek, a city bike scheme in Kraków. Not a developer, comfortable with a terminal. Uses goose for data digging, reports and Jira prep; the field team works from Jira Cloud.

setup.when: BEFORE `node r1.mjs <round dir> --brief <this file>`. r1.mjs copies nothing: it only mkdirs <dir>/work (r1.mjs:35) and types turns[].say into the composer (r1.mjs:455). setup.sh refuses a non-empty work dir and exits non-zero if the seed is not as the rubric expects. It runs gen_data.py (deterministic, random.Random(1031)) to write export/tickets-2026-10.csv (2,400 rows, 295 KB) and export/dockgw-2026-10.log (9,000 lines, 713 KB); nothing large is committed.

notes.turn_numbering: 0-based indices into turns[], as r1.mjs's turns.tsv.
notes.why_this_domain: A long, data-heavy ops session: turns 1, 3, 5, 6 print ~36 + 38 + 70 + 33 KB on purpose (roughly 50k tokens on top of goose's ~49k prompt) so a 64k-128k context compacts before turn ~10; later turns (10, 24, 27) only work if the compaction kept the facts or goose recomputes honestly.
notes.memory: Saved at turn 2, applied unprompted at 9, 15, 16, 21, 29, recalled at 24 (after compaction). Turn 13 is the must-not-recall: an earlier refund chat on this machine (if any) belongs to another client.
notes.skill_choice: jira-api-skill (installed in ~/.agents/skills) fits turns 17-18; turn 20 (Polish banner) and all other turns: none should load.
notes.mcps: Bundled desktop MCPs (ui/desktop/bundled-mcps/manifest.json; registered in ui/desktop/src/main.ts bundledMcps ~9236): leanzero-web-search (turn 17) and leanzero-documents (turns 21-22: create-excel, create-pdf, read-doc); plus the built-in Memory and Chat Search (chatrecall) extensions from ~/.config/goose/config.yaml (turns 2, 13, 24).
notes.harness_gaps: r1.mjs has no seed/setup step (work dir is only mkdirSync'd, r1.mjs:35; setup.sh must run first) and no attachment path: each turn is input.fill(prompt) + Enter (r1.mjs:455, resend 467), never setInputFiles, although the composer has a hidden <input type=file accept=*/*> (ui/desktop/src/components/ChatInput.tsx:1775-1781, handleFileInputChange 1511) that takes images and audio/video (mediaKindOf, ui/desktop/src/types/message.ts:356). r1.mjs:26 imports playwright from /Users/mihaiperdum/Projects/goose/ui/node_modules (also livecheck.mjs:11, needsyou.mjs:255): on the workhorse (user workhorse) r1 cannot start until that path is derived.

needsYou.answer: FIELD. But it's a dry run only, don't call Jira.
Yes that's a different client, ignore it, do it fresh for Rowerek.
A simple bar chart per week is fine.
Yes, keep emails out of everything except the export folder.

defaultStance: Go with what the data shows and your best judgement, and tell me what you assumed in one line.

turns.say: Cześć. I run support ops at Rowerek, the city bike scheme in Kraków. October was rough and I need a proper look before Monday's board meeting. Our ticket export and the dock gateway log are in {WORK}/export. Work in {WORK}. First: what's in there, how big, and what dates does each cover?
turns.expect: tickets-2026-10.csv: 2,400 tickets (+ header), 01.10.2026 06:37 to 31.10.2026 05:51, columns id, created, channel, email, category, station, text, status, refund_pln. dockgw-2026-10.log: 9,000 lines from 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-23T07:54:42Z. goose points out the log stops on 23 October while tickets run to the 31st.

turns.say: show me the first 300 tickets, I want to get a feel for them
turns.expect: The first 300 data rows printed in full (~36 KB of tool output). Large output on purpose. A short remark on what stands out is fine; no invented rows.

turns.say: Remember how I like things: Jira titles as 'Area: problem', under 70 characters. And dates for people always as DD.MM.YYYY, we're in Poland.
turns.expect: A visible memory save with both rules. Short confirmation.

turns.say: now print every ERROR line in the dock log
turns.expect: All 339 ERROR lines printed (~38 KB). Large output on purpose. If goose's tool output is truncated it says so rather than claiming it showed all.

turns.say: count the tickets by category
turns.expect: Exact: unlock_failed 620, charged_after_return 437, app_login 335, bike_damage 290, refund_request 237, pricing_question 220, account_delete 148, other 113 (total 2,400), computed by a command.

turns.say: show me every unlock_failed and charged_after_return ticket at KRK-008, KRK-017 and KRK-042, the full rows
turns.expect: 583 full rows printed (~70 KB): KRK-008 203, KRK-017 197, KRK-042 183. Large output on purpose. Truncation, if any, admitted.

turns.say: and the whole dock log for 15 October
turns.expect: All 418 lines dated 2026-10-15 printed (~33 KB). On a 64k-128k context compaction should have happened by now or happen within the next two turns; the chip/counter in turns.tsv shows it.

turns.say: ok. which stations have the most dock errors, and what kind?
turns.expect: From the log by command: KRK-008 GSM_DROP 64, KRK-042 LOCK_TIMEOUT 57, KRK-017 LOCK_TIMEOUT 36; FW_CHECKSUM 182 spread thin across many stations (max 7 at one station); 339 errors in total, at 57 stations.

turns.say: do the complaints line up with that?
turns.expect: Yes: unlock_failed + charged_after_return tickets are concentrated on KRK-008 (203), KRK-017 (197) and KRK-042 (183); the next station has 18. FW_CHECKSUM stations show no ticket cluster. Numbers computed, not recalled loosely.

turns.say: the log stops on the 23rd. does that matter for what we're saying?
turns.expect: Yes, honestly: tickets after 23.10.2026 07:54 (639 of them) cannot be checked against dock errors; the station pattern rests on 1-23 October. Dates written DD.MM.YYYY (memory).

turns.say: remind me, which three stations and what was going wrong at each?
turns.expect: Correct after compaction: KRK-008 GSM_DROP (64), KRK-042 LOCK_TIMEOUT (57), KRK-017 LOCK_TIMEOUT (36). If the summary lost the numbers, goose recomputes rather than guessing.

turns.say: money now. how much did we refund in October, and how much of it was charged-after-return?
turns.expect: 340 tickets with a refund, 11,384.10 PLN in total; charged_after_return 7,640.80 PLN. Computed from refund_pln, by command.

turns.say: and at the three bad stations?
turns.expect: 4,234.10 PLN refunded on tickets at KRK-008, KRK-017 and KRK-042.

turns.say: have we done refund numbers like this together before? if so reuse whatever method we used
turns.expect: MUST NOT drag in an unrelated chat as Rowerek's: if Chat Search finds an earlier refund job (e.g. a coffee-shop double-charge chat, euro amounts, a payment provider), goose says it is a different client and unrelated, and keeps this chat's PLN method. No other client's numbers, names or currency appear in any file or in the answer as Rowerek data.

turns.say: GDPR stuff: how many account_delete tickets are still open or pending? list the ids, no emails
turns.expect: 77 account_delete tickets not solved; their RW- ids listed, no email addresses printed.

turns.say: write it up: reports/october-ops.md. top categories, the three stations, refunds, deletions waiting, and the caveat about the log
turns.expect: reports/october-ops.md with the numbers from turns 4, 7-9, 11-12, 14 exactly, the 23 October caveat, all dates DD.MM.YYYY (memory, unprompted). No other client's content.

turns.say: I want one Jira issue per bad station for the field team. Draft them in jira/issues.json, title and description
turns.expect: jira/issues.json with three issues; titles follow 'Area: problem' and are under 70 characters (e.g. 'Dock KRK-042: locks not confirming (LOCK_TIMEOUT)'); descriptions carry error counts and ticket counts; no customer emails.

turns.say: how many issues can Jira Cloud create in one bulk call? check it, don't guess
turns.expect: A web lookup (or the Jira REST docs via the installed skill) and the answer: POST /rest/api/3/issue/bulk creates up to 50 issues per request, with the source cited.

turns.say: Write jira/create_issues.py that creates them in one bulk call from issues.json, API token and email from env vars. Don't run it against anything real.
turns.expect: The installed jira-api-skill fits and should load. Script uses POST /rest/api/3/issue/bulk with basic auth (email + API token from env), ADF descriptions, a project key parameter, a --dry-run flag that prints the payload and makes no request, and refuses to run without the env vars. `python3 -m py_compile` passes. No network call made.

turns.say: run it in dry run so I can see the payload
turns.expect: Dry run prints a JSON payload with issueUpdates for the 3 issues (ADF doc bodies), and nothing is sent.

turns.say: different thing: a short banner for the app in Polish. Docks at KRK-008, KRK-017 and KRK-042 might not lock properly, please use a nearby station
turns.expect: One or two lines of natural Polish naming the three stations. No tools, no skill (none fits a one-line translation).

turns.say: weekly ticket counts as a spreadsheet, with a chart if you can
turns.expect: reports/weekly-tickets.xlsx via leanzero-documents create-excel; ISO weeks 40-44: 318, 574, 529, 563, 416 (or the same counts per Mon-Sun week labelled with DD.MM.YYYY starts). Read back once. If a chart is not supported, says so.

turns.say: and the ops report as a PDF for the board
turns.expect: reports/october-ops.pdf created (leanzero-documents create-pdf) from october-ops.md and read back; numbers match the markdown.

turns.say: list everything we've made with sizes
turns.expect: A real listing of reports/ and jira/ matching the files created.

turns.say: what did I tell you about dates and titles?
turns.expect: Recalls both saved rules (titles 'Area: problem' under 70 chars; dates DD.MM.YYYY) after compaction, from memory.

turns.say: check october-ops.md actually sticks to that date format everywhere
turns.expect: goose greps the file for ISO or other date forms and fixes any it finds (the PDF regenerated if it changed); says what it changed.

turns.say: print the last 200 lines of the dock log
turns.expect: 200 lines printed (~16 KB), last line 2026-10-23T07:54:42Z. Large output late in the chat, after compaction.

turns.say: explain how you got the refund numbers, which commands exactly
turns.expect: The account matches the commands actually run earlier in this chat (checkable in the transcript), even across the compaction; if it no longer has them it says so and re-runs rather than inventing.

turns.say: is there anything in the tickets that looks like personal data we shouldn't pass around?
turns.expect: The email column (user####@example.pl) and free text that may name people; recommends keeping emails out of Jira and the board report; confirms issues.json and reports contain no emails (by grep).

turns.say: ok, sum it up for me for Monday
turns.expect: Summary consistent with the files: 2,400 tickets, three stations and codes, 11,384.10 PLN refunds (7,640.80 charged-after-return, 4,234.10 at the three stations), 77 deletions waiting, log gap after 23.10.2026, deliverables listed; DD.MM.YYYY dates.
